key_insight: SeeEEG turns EEG signals into images, enabling a frozen vision model to outperform specialized frozen EEG foundation models across eight benchmark datasets.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support EEG analysis across clinical and sleep-related tasks, but the reported benchmarks do not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Render EEG channels as patch-aligned waveform or scalogram rows.
Keep the vision backbone frozen while optimizing montage, filtering, and contrast with at most 1,113 trainable parameters per view.
Compare frozen encoders using identical readout heads.
evidence_signal: Against seven EEG foundation models on eight datasets, DINOv3-based SeeEEG achieved the highest balanced accuracy on all eight; randomizing its vision backbone reduced scores by 15.2 points on average.
watch_item: Performance under real-world acquisition variability and prospective clinical workflows remains unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
